Challenging judgment and award dated 13.11.2014 passed by Senior Civil Judge and Addl. MACT at Shorapur, sitting at Shahapur (for short 'Tribunal'), in MVC no.10/2012, this appeal is filed.

sentences.text: Smt.Sangeeta Bhadrashetty, learned counsel for appellant submitted that appeal was filed by insurer challenging award of Tribunal on finding regarding liability as well as quantum.

It was submitted that in an accident that occurred on 13.08.2011, Mahadevamma and others travelling in a passenger auto rickshaw bearing registration no.KA-33/7467 sustained grievous injuries, when its driver drove it in rash and negligent manner on Alkur-Kadamgera road and dashed against an on coming motorcycle and thereafter turtled.
It was stated that Mahadevamma died during treatment at hospital.
Alleging loss of dependency, her husband and children filed claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act against owner and insurer of auto rickshaw and rider of motorcycle.
3. Despite service of notice, owner did not enter appearance and contest.
He was place ex-parte.
Insurer filed objections denying entire claim petition averments.

It was specifically pleaded that accident occurred beyond NC: 2023:KHC-K:6438 geographical limit of 8 kms. of Shahapur town fixed in permit and therefore, terms and conditions of policy were violated.
A plea of violation of other policy conditions was also made.
Respondent no.3 - rider of motorcycle contended that police investigation records were implicating driver of auto rickshaw for causing accident and sought for dismissal of claim petition.
4. Based on pleadings, Tribunal framed issues and recorded evidence.
Claimant no.1 was examined as PW.1 and an eyewitness to accident as PW.2.
Exs. P1
to P8 were marked.
Insurer examined its official as RW.1 and ARTO as RW.2.
Exs. R1
to R4 were got marked.
5. On consideration, Tribunal held that accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of auto rickshaw by its driver and deceased Mahadevamma sustained fatal injuries in said accident.
It also held that insurance policy issued was valid on date of accident and insurer was liable to pay compensation.
It was submitted that said award was unsustainable.

It was specifically NC:
2023:KHC-K:6438 contended that accident spot as per police investigation records was in Hanchinal village, which was nearly 30 kms. from limits of Shahapur town.
In Ex.R4 - permit issued to vehicle, it was prohibited from plying beyond 8 kms. from limits of Shahapur town.

Therefore,
there was clear violation of policy conditions and insurer was entitled to seek for discharge of its liability.
6. Insofar as quantum of compensation, it was submitted that as per post mortem report, age of deceased Mahadevamma was recorded as 50 years.
However, Tribunal erred in adding 30% future prospects instead of 10%.

It was also contended that, Tribunal awarded Rs.50,000/- towards loss of consortium, Rs.50,000/- towards loss of love and affection, Rs.25,000/- towards funeral expenses and Rs.10,000/- towards transportation of dead body, which were excessive as per ratio in case of National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi and others reported NC: 2023:KHC-K:6438 in (2017) 16 SCC 680

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel, perused impugned judgment and award and record.
9. From above submission, it is seen that only insurer is in appeal challenging finding of Tribunal on liability as well as quantum of compensation.

Therefore, points that arise for consideration are:
"1.
Whether finding of Tribunal regarding liability of insurer to pay compensation calls for interference?
2. Whether compensation awarded by Tribunal calls for reduction?"

NC: 2023:KHC-K:6438 POINT NO.1:
10.

Main ground for challenging finding of Tribunal on liability is, as per Ex.R4, insured vehicle was required to be plied within 8 kms. from Shahapur town limits, but accident occurred near Hanchinal village, which was beyond said limit as deposed by RW.2 - ARTO.
However, whether accident spot was beyond 8 kms. of town limits of Shahapur and whether there was violation of policy conditions would be a question of fact.
Insurer has sought to establish same by examining its official and ARTO.
On perusal of deposition of RW.1, it is seen that assertion about distance of accident spot and town limit is not on basis of his own experience or knowledge.
Same would render it unreliable.
Spot panchanama of accident is not produced.

Though ARTO is examined as RW.2, he has contradicted his statement in examination-in-chief about distance between Kadamgera and Shahapur town as 30 kms. by admitting that his department was not competent to depose about distance between two places.
In view of NC: 2023:KHC-K:6438 said admission, lone material based on which contention was sought to be substantiated is rendered ineffective.
Even in Ex.R1 - Legal Notice issued to insured by insurer, there is no mention about violation of permit limit.

Under such circumstances,
since insurer has not led specific evidence to establish that accident occurred when vehicle was plying beyond geographical permit area, finding of Tribunal against insurer cannot be found fault with.
Point no.1 is therefore answered in negative.

POINT NO.2:
11.
There is no dispute about death of Mahadevamma, a house wife aged 50 years and claimants were husband and children, younger of whom is shown as student aged 24 years.

As per ratio laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Pranay Sethi (supra), since deceased was aged 50 years and self-employed, future prospects at 10% is required to be added, deduction towards personal expenses would be '1/3rd' and multiplier applicable would be '13'.

Tribunal has considered her NC:
2023:KHC-K:6438 monthly income at Rs.6,000/-.

Therefore, compensation towards loss of dependency would be:
Rs.6,000 + 10% x 12 x 13 x 2/3 = Rs.6,86,400/-.
12.

Apart from above, as per decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram and others reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130 and in United India Insurance Co. Ltd., v. Satinder Kaur alias Satwinder Kaur and others,
reported in AIR 2020 SC 3076, claimant no.1 being husband of deceased would be entitled to Rs.40,000/- towards spousal consortium and claimants no.2 and 3 being sons would be entitled to Shriram General Insurance Co.Ltd vs Ayyappa S/O Padmanna Doddamani on 14 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37340666/
4 Rs.40,000/- each towards loss of filial consortium.

Since three years have been lapsed, they would be entitled for addition of 10% on award under conventional heads.
Point no.2 is answered partly in affirmative as above.

Consequently, following:
ORDER i. Appeal is allowed-in-part with costs.
ii. Compensation awarded by Tribunal is reduced from Rs.9,03,000/- to Rs.8,51,400/-.
iii. Amount in deposit is ordered to be transmitted to Tribunal for payment.
iv. Appellant-insurer shall deposit balance compensation within six weeks from date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
v. On deposit and since respondent no.1 i.e., claimant no.1 has died during pendency of appeal, compensation shall be shared between claimants no.2 and 3 equally.
